## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the Marchenko-Pastur edges and the Ledoit-Wolf criterion from memory.
- Say which estimator you would use for 50 assets, for 500, and for 3,000, with the reason for each.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 106 to 111. The positive-definiteness test across all rolling windows is the piece worth having green, because it is what stops an optimiser failing silently in phase 10.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Closed book: the Marchenko-Pastur edges in terms of the ratio, the shrinkage criterion, the parameter counts of the four estimators, and your selection rule by universe size. One page.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, sixteenth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 1/0.85 and 1/1.15 to three decimals.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Martingales and optional stopping: a gambler with 100 units bets one unit on fair coin flips and stops at 0 or 200. Use the martingale property to get the ruin probability in one line, then say which of the optional stopping conditions you relied on.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> The version with a drift: same game, but the coin pays with probability 0.48. Find the martingale that works here and use it. This one is asked directly and the trick is finding the right exponential.
:::
:::
